facts.statement: Hoazinoides is an extinct bird genus found in the Middle Miocene "Monkey Beds" of La Venta, Colombia.
facts.quote: Hoazinoides is an extinct genus of birds from the Middle Miocene (Laventan) from the "Monkey Beds" of the Villavieja Formation of the Honda Group at the Konzentrat-Lagerstätte of La Venta, Colombia.

facts.statement: The only known species of this genus is Hoazinoides magdalenae.
facts.quote: The only known species is Hoazinoides magdalenae.

facts.statement: This bird was similar in shape to the modern hoatzin but smaller, with a concave parietal skull wall and unfused coracoid and sternum.
facts.quote: From these remains it appears that this bird was similar to that of hoatzin, although smaller, and distinguished from it in the parietal wall of the skull is concave and the coracoid and sternum were not fused.

facts.statement: Its feet resembled those of modern owls, featuring a fourth toe that could rotate backwards.
facts.quote: Its feet were like those of modern owls, in which the fourth toe can rotate backwards.

facts.statement: Tab Rasmussen erected the family Hoazinoididae for this genus in 1997 due to its unique skeletal features.
facts.quote: This is why Tab Rasmussen (1997) erected a new family, Hoazinoididae, for it.

facts.statement: Some experts do not consider it part of the hoatzin family (Opisthocomidae) and created the separate family Hoazinoididae, leaving its exact relationship to modern hoatzins uncertain.
facts.quote: motivo por el cual algunos expertos no le consideran parte de la familia de los hoacines (Opisthocomidae) y se le creó una familia particular, Hoazinoididae, dentro de los cuculiformes, dejando en el aire la cuestión de su parentesco exacto con sus símiles modernos.

facts.statement: Hoazinoides is an extinct bird genus belonging to the order Cuculiformes, which includes modern cuckoos and hoatzins.
facts.quote: Hoazinoides es un género extinto de ave del orden de los cuculiformes, que comprende a los modernos cucos y a los hoacines.

facts.statement: Hoazinoides lived during the Middle Miocene (Laventan) in Colombia.
facts.quote: Hoazinoides is an extinct genus of birds from the Middle Miocene (Laventan) from the "Monkey Beds" of the Villavieja Formation of the Honda Group at the Konzentrat-Lagerstätte of La Venta, Colombia.

facts.statement: The fossils date to the middle of the Miocene period.
facts.quote: que datan de mediados del período Mioceno.

facts.statement: The time range for Hoazinoides is from 15.98 to 10 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Langhian to Tortonian (15.98 to 10 million years ago)

facts.statement: Remains suggest its arms had adaptations similar to hoatzins for hooking onto tree branches, a necessity in a jungle environment for a bird of low mobility.
facts.quote: Adicionalmente, restos de su ulna o cúbito distal y del carpo-metacarpo sugieren que sus brazos presentaban adaptaciones similares a las de los hoacines para poder engancharse a las ramas de los árboles, algo necesario en un ambiente selvático para un ave de escasa movilidad.

facts.statement: The genus was described by Miller in 1953.
The genus authority is A. H. Miller, 1953.

rejected.statement: The genus name refers to its resemblance to the modern hoatzin, while the species name refers to its discovery near the Magdalena River basin.
rejected.quote: Its generic epithet refers to its resemblance to modern hoatzin, and its specific name refers to its discovery near the Magdalena River basin.

rejected.statement: Hoazinoides is known from fragmentary remains including the back of the skull, specimen UCMP 42823, and limb bones.
rejected.quote: Like many other fossil birds, it is known from fragmentary remains, including the back portion of the skull, the specimen UCMP 42823 and other bones of the extremities.

rejected.quote: Additionally, the remains of its distal ulna and carpal-metacarpal suggest that its arms were similar to those of hoatzins.
